unitChecks.reason: Names the subject 慕容皝 as Murong Huang in both fields.
Gives courtesy name 元真 and third-son relation to 慕容廆 correctly in both fields.
龍顏版齒 is dragon countenance and plaque teeth; 七尺八寸 are chi and cun, not English feet and inches.
Covers 雄毅多權略, esteem for 經學, and skill in 天文 without dropping a proposition.
States that when 廆 was Duke of Liaodong, Huang was established as 世子.
Keeps Jianwu appointment cluster: 冠軍將軍, 左賢王, 望平侯, and repeated campaign merit.
Keeps late Taining 平北將軍 and advance to 朝鮮公.
Covers succession on 廆卒, acting 平州刺史, and 督攝部內 authority.
Tracks Qidegui expelled by Yidougui, Huang’s cavalry, peace request, and two cities built.
Distinguishes 庶兄翰 from 母弟仁、昭 and Huang’s jealousy and displeasure.
States that after Hui’s death they all feared they could not preserve themselves.
Han flees to Duan Liao; Ren urges Zhao to raise troops and depose Huang.
遇仁於險瀆 follows 遣使按檢: the envoys met Ren at Xiandu, not an ambiguous subject that could read as Huang.
東歸平郭 is returning east to Pingguo, not merely fleeing east; 知事發 is knowing the affair had broken.
Names 建武幼 and 司馬佟壽 among those sent to campaign against Ren.
Ren commits his full host; You’s side is greatly defeated and lost to Ren.
Lists Liaodong rebels and the officers who abandoned their cities and fled back.
Ren holds all east of the Liao and self-styles the chariot-cavalry and ducal titles.
鮮卑諸部 means the various Xianbei divisions or tribes, not “other Xianbei chiefs.”
EN drops the 揚威 title before 淑虞 and understates 皆斬之 as taking heads without the paired beheading.
材官劉佩 attacks Yilian and fails to take it.
Duan Liao raids Tuhe; Zhang Meng meets and defeats him.
遼弟蘭 marks Lan as Liao’s younger brother; 寇/擊敗 are raid and defeat, not a vague ‘until driven off.’
Distinguishes the second Murong Han (甯遠) sent with Feng Yi to relieve Liucheng.
The supplied EN quote omits 難與爭鋒, 宜顧萬全, and 慎勿輕進 as distinct admonitions in Huang’s warning.
千餘騎 is over a thousand cavalry, not ‘a thousand,’ and 死者大半 is more than half dead.
Lan’s ladders and tunnels, twenty-day siege, Shi Cong’s sortie, 1500 heads, Lan flees.
Emperor Cheng’s credentialed investiture mirrors Hui’s 持節都督承制 bundle.
Huang personally campaigns Liaodong and takes Xiangping.
Liu Cheng surrenders Juqiu; Zhang Heng seizes the magistrate and surrenders.
Executes Ren’s magistrates, moves great clans to Jicheng, sets three counties, returns.
Early Xiankang Feng Yi raids Sheyiyu’s Yuwen separate division and returns with spoils.
又敗之 after Feng Yi’s prior victory means Sheyiyu was again defeated, not that Sheyiyu defeated ‘them.’
Advisers remonstrate that the sea route is perilous and urge the land route.
舊海水無淩 is that the sea formerly had no ice, not that it ‘seldom froze’; 凍合者三矣 is three freezes.
Keeps Guangwu/Hutuo ice exemplum and Heaven’s possible intent to destroy Ren.
Closes the speech: plan decided; whoever obstructs is to be beheaded.
Leads the three armies from Changli treading the ice to advance.
軍去平郭七里 is the army, not a ‘vanguard’; EN omits 候騎乃告 and 殺仁而還.
Establishes the ritual 藉田 east of Chaoyang Gate with offices to manage it.
遣將李詠 is Liao sending general Li Yong; EN also drops 都尉 for Zhang Meng and the withdraw-then-pursue sequence.
Lan camps tens of thousands at Qushui; Yuwen Gui raids Anjin as support.
Fifty thousand strike; when the army halts at Liucheng, Lan and Gui flee.
EN omits 遣, the defeat 敗之, and the return 而還 after 館穀二旬.
Predicts the two foes will return in force; ambush to be set beside Liucheng.
Feng Yi’s cavalry is to lurk on the Ma’er Mountain roads.
Liao’s cavalry arrives; pincer defeat; general Rong Bao is beheaded.
兼長史 and 郎中令 are explicit offices for Liu Bin and Yang Jing; EN drops both roles.
攻宇文別部 is a separate Yuwen division, not undifferentiated ‘the Yuwen’; 使其/伐 structure is also flattened.
Sets up the remonstrance board to open the path of blunt speech.
徙昌黎郡 relocates Changli commandery; it is not Huang shifting his own seat to Changli; EN also drops 將軍 and 以逼乙連.
Also walls Qushui as support for Lan Bo.
Yilian starves; Liao’s grain convoy is intercepted and taken by Lan Bo.
遼遣將 and 皝將 are omitted; 雲敗，斬之 is defeat then beheading, not a vague ‘destroyed.’
Heavy burden/light rank advice; Xiankang 3 illegitimate kingship and pardon.
Appoints Feng Yi chancellor, Han Shou marshal, and the listed ministers/generals.
Wenchang Hall, gold-root carriage, six horses, and 警蹕 clearance on movement.
其妻 and 世子 are explicit; 輔政故事 is the assisting-government precedent, not a bare name citation.
Because Liao is a repeated border trouble, Song Hui declares vassalage and asks troops.
Shi Hu / Jilong assembles his host and arrives.
Attacks north of Lingzhi; defeats Duan Lan; thousands of heads; 5000+ households.
Shi Hu reaches Xuwu; Liao flees to Miyun Mountain.
四面進攻 is attack from all four sides; 郡縣諸部叛應…三十六城 is prefectures, counties, and divisions, not only ‘towns.’
After standing off over ten days, attendants urge Huang to surrender.
Huang refuses surrender, saying he means to take All under Heaven.
子恪等 is his son Ke and others, not plural ‘sons Ke’; 晨出擊之 is a dawn sortie that struck them.
Shi Hu’s armies panic, cast armor, and flee.
Ke pursues, takes 30,000+, builds a garrison at Fancheng, and returns.
Duan Liao feigns surrender to Shi Hu and asks troops to meet him.
Ma Qiu ambushed by Ke’s 7000; Yang Yu and Xianyu Liang captured; Liao brought back.
Advance to 征北大將軍 and Youzhou shepherd, concurrent Pingzhou, added offices and fief.
Murong Ping defeats Shi Cheng’s side in Liaoxi; slays two generals; takes 1000+ households.
Duan Liao plots rebellion and Huang executes him.

additionalCorrections.before: He had an imperial bearing, unusually square teeth, and stood seven feet eight inches tall.
additionalCorrections.after: He had a dragon countenance and plaque-like teeth, and stood seven chi eight cun tall.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 龍顏版齒，身長七尺八寸。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 龍顏版齒 is dragon countenance and plaque teeth; 七尺八寸 are chi and cun, not English feet and inches.

additionalCorrections.before: Huang killed Zhao, sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation, met Ren at Xiandu.
additionalCorrections.after: Huang killed Zhao and sent envoys to investigate the truth of Ren’s situation; they met Ren at Xiandu.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝殺昭，遣使按檢仁之虛實，遇仁於險瀆。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 遇仁於險瀆 follows 遣使按檢: the envoys met Ren at Xiandu, not an ambiguous subject that could read as Huang.

additionalCorrections.before: Ren saw his plot exposed, killed the messenger, and fled east to Pingguo.
additionalCorrections.after: Ren knew the affair had come out; he killed Huang’s envoy and returned east to Pingguo.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 仁知事發，殺皝使，東歸平郭。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 東歸平郭 is returning east to Pingguo, not merely fleeing east; 知事發 is knowing the affair had broken.

additionalCorrections.before: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and other Xianbei chiefs backed him.
additionalCorrections.after: Yuwen Gui, Duan Liao, and the various Xianbei divisions all backed him.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 宇文歸、段遼及鮮卑諸部並為之援，
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 鮮卑諸部 means the various Xianbei divisions or tribes, not “other Xianbei chiefs.”

additionalCorrections.before: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent Marshal Feng Yi to strike the Xianbei leader Muti at Bailang and Shuyu to strike the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both enemy heads were taken.
additionalCorrections.after: In the ninth year of Xianhe, Huang sent his marshal Feng Yi to attack the Xianbei Muti at Bailang, and the Yangwei general Shuyu to attack the Wuhuan Siluohou at Pinggang; both were beheaded.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 咸和九年，皝遣其司馬封弈攻鮮卑木堤于白狼，揚威淑虞攻烏丸悉羅侯于平岡，皆斬之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: EN drops the 揚威 title before 淑虞 and understates 皆斬之 as taking heads without the paired beheading.

additionalCorrections.before: Duan Lan and Murong Han attacked Liucheng until commandant Shi Cong drove them off.
additionalCorrections.after: Liao’s younger brother Lan together with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 遼弟蘭與翰寇柳城，都尉石琮擊敗之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 遼弟蘭 marks Lan as Liao’s younger brother; 寇/擊敗 are raid and defeat, not a vague ‘until driven off.’

additionalCorrections.before: Huang warned Murong Han (the general of pacifying distance): “The foe is numerous and keen—do not trade blows rashly; wait until your force is formed, then attack.”
additionalCorrections.after: Huang warned Han, saying: “The bandits’ host is numerous and their spirit keen; it is hard to contend at the spear-tip. You ought to look to complete safety, and carefully do not advance lightly; you must wait until the troops are gathered and the lines set, then strike them.”
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝戒汗曰：「賊眾氣銳，難與爭鋒，宜顧萬全，慎勿輕進，必須兵集陣整，然後擊之。」
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The supplied EN quote omits 難與爭鋒, 宜顧萬全, and 慎勿輕進 as distinct admonitions in Huang’s warning.

additionalCorrections.before: Murong Han was impetuous: he sent a thousand horse ahead as a van, ignored Feng Yi’s warning, and was routed by Duan Lan with heavy losses.
additionalCorrections.after: Han’s nature was fierce and keen; he dispatched over a thousand cavalry as a vanguard to advance; Feng Yi stopped him, but Han did not follow, was defeated by Lan, and the dead were more than half.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 汗性驍銳，遣千餘騎為前鋒而進，封弈止之，汗不從，為蘭所敗，死者大半。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 千餘騎 is over a thousand cavalry, not ‘a thousand,’ and 死者大半 is more than half dead.

additionalCorrections.before: Sheyiyu led cavalry to pursue battle at Hunshui; again defeated them.
additionalCorrections.after: Sheyiyu led cavalry to pursue battle at the Hun River and was again defeated.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 涉奕于率騎追戰于渾水，又敗之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 又敗之 after Feng Yi’s prior victory means Sheyiyu was again defeated, not that Sheyiyu defeated ‘them.’

additionalCorrections.before: Huang replied, “This gulf seldom froze in the past, yet since Ren’s revolt it has frozen solid three winters running.
additionalCorrections.after: Huang said, “Formerly the sea water had no ice; since Ren’s rebellion, the freeze has joined three times.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 皝曰：「舊海水無淩，自仁反已來，凍合者三矣。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 舊海水無淩 is that the sea formerly had no ice, not that it ‘seldom froze’; 凍合者三矣 is three freezes.

additionalCorrections.before: Ren never expected him: Huang’s vanguard was seven li from Pingguo before Ren learned of it; Ren scrambled into battle, was taken, and executed.
additionalCorrections.after: Ren did not expect Huang’s arrival; the army was seven li from Pingguo when scout riders reported it; Ren came out to fight in confusion, was captured by Huang, who killed Ren and returned.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 仁不虞皝之至也，軍去平郭七里，候騎乃告，仁狼狽出戰，為皝所擒，殺仁而還。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 軍去平郭七里 is the army, not a ‘vanguard’; EN omits 候騎乃告 and 殺仁而還.

additionalCorrections.before: Duan Liao’s night raid on Wuxing failed in the rain; Zhang Meng ran down Li Yong and captured him.
additionalCorrections.after: Duan Liao sent general Li Yong to night-raid Wuxing; meeting rain, he withdrew; commandant Zhang Meng pursued and captured Yong.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 段遼遣將李詠夜襲武興，遇雨，引還，都尉張萌追擊，擒詠。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 遣將李詠 is Liao sending general Li Yong; EN also drops 都尉 for Zhang Meng and the withdraw-then-pursue sequence.

additionalCorrections.before: Feng Yi chased with light horse, seized their supplies, and fed his men from enemy granaries for twenty days.
additionalCorrections.after: He sent Feng Yi leading light cavalry in pursuit; Feng defeated them, gathered their military stores, lodged on their grain for twenty days, and returned.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 遣封弈率輕騎追擊，敗之，收其軍實，館穀二旬而還。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: EN omits 遣, the defeat 敗之, and the return 而還 after 館穀二旬.

additionalCorrections.before: He sent Liu Bin and Yang Jing to escort Xu Meng’s party to the capital.
additionalCorrections.after: He sent concurrent chief clerk Liu Bin and palace director Yang Jing to escort Xu Meng and others back to the capital.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 遣兼長史劉斌、郎中令陽景送徐孟等歸於京師。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 兼長史 and 郎中令 are explicit offices for Liu Bin and Yang Jing; EN drops both roles.

additionalCorrections.before: His heir Murong Jun stormed Duan Liao’s towns while Feng Yi struck the Yuwen—both returned in triumph.
additionalCorrections.after: He had his heir apparent Jun campaign against Duan Liao’s cities, and Feng Yi attack a separate Yuwen division; both returned in great victory.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 使其世子俊伐段遼諸城，封弈攻宇文別部，皆大捷而歸。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 攻宇文別部 is a separate Yuwen division, not undifferentiated ‘the Yuwen’; 使其/伐 structure is also flattened.

additionalCorrections.before: He shifted his seat to Changli, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and stationed Lan Bo there to choke the enemy.
additionalCorrections.after: He later relocated Changli commandery, built Haocheng east of Yilian, and had general Lan Bo garrison it to press Yilian.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 後徙昌黎郡，築好城于乙連東，使將軍蘭勃戍之，以逼乙連。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 徙昌黎郡 relocates Changli commandery; it is not Huang shifting his own seat to Changli; EN also drops 將軍 and 以逼乙連.

additionalCorrections.before: Qu Yun attacked Xingguo but Murong Zun destroyed him at Wuguan River and took his entire force.
additionalCorrections.after: Liao sent general Qu Yun to attack Xingguo; Yun fought a great battle with Huang’s general Murong Zun at Wuguan River, was defeated and beheaded, and his entire force was captured.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 遼遣將屈雲攻興國，與皝將慕容遵大戰于五官水上，雲敗，斬之，盡俘其眾。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 遼遣將 and 皝將 are omitted; 雲敗，斬之 is defeat then beheading, not a vague ‘destroyed.’

additionalCorrections.before: He made Lady Duan queen and Murong Jun crown prince, citing Cao Cao and Sima Zhao as precedents.
additionalCorrections.after: He made his wife Lady Duan queen and the heir apparent Jun crown prince, all following the Wei Wu and Jin Wen precedents of assisting in government.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 以其妻段氏為王后，世子俊為太子，皆如魏武、晉文輔政故事。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 其妻 and 世子 are explicit; 輔政故事 is the assisting-government precedent, not a bare name citation.

additionalCorrections.before: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not coordinated, drove on to Jicheng with hundreds of thousands of men; thirty-six towns went over to him.
additionalCorrections.after: Shi Hu entered Lingzhi, furious that Huang had not joined forces, advanced to strike him as far as Jicheng; several hundred thousand troops attacked from all four sides, and thirty-six cities among the prefectures, counties, and various divisions rebelled in response to Shi Hu.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 季龍進入令支，怒皝之不會師也，進軍擊之，至於棘城，戎卒數十萬，四面進攻，郡縣諸部叛應季龍者三十六城。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 四面進攻 is attack from all four sides; 郡縣諸部叛應…三十六城 is prefectures, counties, and divisions, not only ‘towns.’

additionalCorrections.before: Sent sons Ke and others leading cavalry two thousand, dawn sortie struck them.
additionalCorrections.after: Sent his son Ke and others leading two thousand cavalry; at dawn they sortied and struck them.
additionalCorrections.sourceQuote: 遣子恪等率騎二千，晨出擊之。
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 子恪等 is his son Ke and others, not plural ‘sons Ke’; 晨出擊之 is a dawn sortie that struck them.

recordCorrections.sourceQuote: 雄毅多權略，尚經學，善天文。
recordCorrections.sourceReason: 尚經學 means Huang esteemed classical learning; ‘studied’ understates 尚 as mere study.
